content: For individuals over 12 years of age, administer 15 to 60 mL orally as a single dose. For children aged 2 to 12 years, administer 5 to 15 mL orally as a single dose. For children under 2 years of age, administer 1 to 5 mL orally as a single dose. If the medication is being used prior to a procedure, administer 15 to 60 mL orally as a single dose, 16 hours before the procedure. Potential side effects include dizziness, abdominal cramps, diarrhea, nausea, electrolyte disturbances, hypotension, pelvic congestion, and hypersensitivity reactions. This medication should not be used for longer than one week. Consult a healthcare professional if you experience abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, or a sudden change in bowel movements that persists for more than two weeks. If you are taking other medications, consult a healthcare professional, as this product should be taken at least two hours before or after other drugs to avoid interactions. Laxatives may alter the effectiveness of other medications. If you experience rectal bleeding or fail to have a bowel movement after use, discontinue the medication and consult a healthcare professional. It is important to seek advice from a healthcare professional before using this product, especially during pregnancy. This medication is generally considered acceptable for use during pregnancy, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk.
